sources.title: Copilot in the cloud
sources.locator: Environment comparison; ways to work; limitations
sources.finding: GitHub distinguishes cloud sandboxes from Actions-based sessions, including repository scope, compute controls, shared logs and a 59-minute Actions limit.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
sources.locator: Supported OS; modes; sandboxing; GitHub tasks
sources.finding: The CLI runs interactively or by prompt, supports local/cloud sandbox modes and structured planning, and can act on GitHub issues and PRs.

sources.title: Plans for GitHub Copilot
sources.locator: Plan overview; individual plans; credit allowances
sources.finding: The current plan table uses GitHub AI credits and separates free chat/client access from paid cloud work.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot app
sources.finding: Copilot app supports macOS, Linux and Windows, separate worktrees/branches, parallel sessions and PR review/merge workflows. Organization policy governs access.

sources.title: GitHub Mobile
sources.finding: GitHub Mobile ships Android and iOS apps and supports Copilot chat and assigning issues to Copilot.

sources.title: Cloud sandboxes
sources.finding: Cloud sandboxes run isolated Linux sessions without needing the client connected. Multiple sessions run in parallel; stopped sessions retain snapshots and resume files. GitHub Actions remains a separate environment option.

sources.title: Creating a custom environment
sources.finding: Users can register a Linux host or codespace as a custom execution environment. The user operates the host, workspace and dependencies. Closing a client does not stop the machine.

sources.title: Delegating and parallelizing
sources.finding: /fleet makes the main agent orchestrate subtasks and dependencies, run independent children concurrently and combine results. Each child uses its own context and additional model usage.

sources.title: Copilot App projects
sources.finding: Projects retain ongoing goals, conversations, artifacts and recurring work. Overview groups Needs input, Open, Working and Done. Users inspect plans, changes and PRs and steer sessions.

sources.title: Copilot automations
sources.finding: Paid-plan automations trigger on schedules, repository events or API requests. Per-run credit controls and repository write scope are configurable; shared automation visibility/editing follows repository permissions.

sources.title: Copilot issue creation and updates
sources.finding: In public preview, Copilot creates or updates GitHub issues from prompts/images, including title, body, labels and assignees. Humans review drafts before submission.

sources.title: Third-party coding agents
sources.finding: Paid Copilot plans support public-preview Claude Agent SDK and Codex SDK coding agents. These are named coding-agent integrations, not only models. GitHub policy must enable each partner separately.

sources.title: Copilot CLI Authentication
sources.locator: Unauthenticated use; Offline mode; OAuth SSO
sources.finding: BYOK requires no GitHub account. COPILOT_OFFLINE=true avoids GitHub services and fully disables telemetry; only the configured provider remains. Complete airgap requires a local/in-network model. OAuth can authorize SAML organizations.

sources.title: Agent management for enterprises
sources.finding: Enterprise owners, AI managers and organization owners control Copilot and partner-agent policies at different scopes. Enterprise audit logs can track agentic activity; partner policies are separate from Copilot.

sources.title: Additional Product Terms
sources.finding: Copilot use is governed by GitHub Generative AI Services Terms for direct Business/Enterprise purchases, Microsoft Product Terms for Microsoft purchases, or GitHub Terms AI section otherwise.
